title: Materialize console launcher into user projects at init
description: The /hivemind:console command ships and works in any installed project, but the double-click launchers (console.cmd / console.sh) live only in the framework dev repo root. A non-technical user who installs the plugin into their own project has no double-click way to open the console there. Make bin/init.js materialize console.cmd and console.sh into the user's project root so they can launch the console without the terminal, mirroring the existing workflows/agents materializer pattern (never-overwrite, idempotent). Also surface the /console command + double-click launcher in the init quickstart/README output so it is discoverable. NOTE: bin/init.js is bundled to dist/init.cjs — rebuild via npm run build:plugin and commit the updated bundle; the dist-parity gate (TASK-049) runs under npm run test:all, which is the required gate for this ticket since it touches bundled source.
acceptance_criteria: Running bin/init.js on a fresh project writes console.cmd and console.sh into the user's project root (resolved from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, falling back to cwd), each launching node "<dist>/task-board.cjs" --open --port 4517 the same way the dev-repo launchers do.

Materialization is never-overwrite and idempotent: an existing console.cmd/console.sh in the project is left untouched, and a second init run adds nothing and reports it skipped (matches the workflows materializer contract).
The init branches behave correctly: launchers are materialized on fresh-create (and --force) but the already_initialized branch performs no launcher mutation.

The launcher content is shipped from the plugin (not hand-duplicated in init logic) so the dev-repo console.cmd/console.sh and the materialized copies stay byte-consistent, with a parity test locking it.
The quickstart/README (or init stdout) tells the user they can double-click console.cmd / run sh console.sh, or use /hivemind:console, to open the console.
dist/init.cjs is rebuilt (npm run build:plugin) and committed; npm run test:all passes (fast + slow tiers, including dist-parity).
